clue.text: Surprisingly, EEC bans time off work

indicators.note: letters arranged in a surprising way are not in the order printed

explanation.surface: A startled report that the European Economic Community has outlawed days off.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitals make EEC look like an institution, but they are just three letters of fodder; the EEC was the forerunner of the EU.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the workplace sense: an absence on a staff record is a day not spent at work.

clue.text: Holds party for politicians at house with press regularly

parts.note: the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party
HO is the standard abbreviation for house

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals from 'press' keeps the second and fourth

explanation.surface: Someone throws a political party at their home and invites the press along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds party' reads as hosting an event, but 'Holds' is the definition on its own and 'party' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To anchor something is to hold it fast in place, so anchors means holds.

clue.text: Concede part concealing sin retrospectively

parts.note: to sunder is to part or split apart

indicators.note: looking back over something reads it from the end

explanation.surface: An admission that one side hid its misdeeds after the fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part' is a verb here, not a noun: SUNDER, which is split open to take the backwards sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an army that surrenders concedes defeat, and in an argument you can surrender a point just as you concede it.

clue.text: Lowest point of drain is broken

indicators.note: something broken falls apart and its letters can be put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A plumbing disaster: the bottom of the drain has cracked.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as the lowest point of a pipe, which is neat because a nadir is exactly that.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym from astronomy, where the nadir is the point directly beneath the observer, now used for the worst moment of anything.

clue.text: Winning finish gets attention in golf

parts.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A golfer's victorious final hole draws the crowd's attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning finish' looks like one phrase about victory, but 'Winning' is the definition in its charming sense and 'finish' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A winning smile is an endearing one: both mean charming.

clue.text: Lawyers earn a good deal

parts.note: to gain money is to earn it

explanation.surface: The old grumble that lawyers make plenty of money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A good deal' reads as 'a lot' of money, but it is the definition in its shopping sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargain is a good deal, something bought cheaply.

clue.text: Sudden outbreak of resistance during raid

parts.note: a police raid is a bust
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Fighting breaks out when the police raid meets resistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outbreak of resistance' reads as one phrase, but the definition stops at 'outbreak'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a burst of applause or of gunfire breaks out all at once.

clue.text: Paddy's piece of land supports cereal

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting word sits underneath

parts.note: a field is a piece of land

explanation.surface: An Irishman named Paddy owns a plot that grows cereal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddy's' looks like a man's name in the possessive, but it is the flooded field; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddy is a flooded field where rice is grown.

clue.text: Not right having tantrums becoming older

explanation.surface: A grumpy remark that throwing tantrums is unbecoming as one gets older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not right' reads as 'wrong', but it splits: 'right' is R and 'Not' removes it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aging, also spelt ageing, means becoming older.

clue.text: Refusal by navy vessels to return without a break

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for navy

indicators.note: going back the way they came, the vessels read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: The navy refuses to let its ships come home for a rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessels' suggests ships in a naval surface, but here they are kitchen pots.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a nonstop flight or party runs from start to finish with no pause.

clue.text: Tended to worry over daughter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A parent was inclined to fret about their daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tended to' reads as 'was inclined to', but 'Tended' means looked after and 'to' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To tend the sick is to care for them, so tended means cared.

clue.text: Setter working to follow unambiguous guidance

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as I
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: The crossword setter is busy producing clear instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter is the person who wrote the clue, so 'Setter' gives I.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a team that lacks direction lacks leadership and instruction, and working under someone's direction means following their lead.

clue.text: Have an OTT response concerning misplaced crate

parts.note: a row over money is a row concerning money

indicators.note: misplaced letters are out of their proper order

explanation.surface: Someone throws a fit because a crate has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT means 'over the top', excessive; the definition is the whole phrase before 'concerning'.
explanation.definitionFit: To overreact is to respond more strongly than the situation warrants.

clue.text: Struggle with vision after change of leader

explanation.surface: Someone battles poor eyesight after a shake-up at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter replaces S; the definition supplies it, so this is solved from 'Struggle' and checked against SIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, as verb or noun: fighting for breath is struggling for it.

clue.text: Dull at the margins within state, unfortunately

indicators.note: the margins are the edges, so only the outer letters of 'Dull' are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of Dull

explanation.surface: A regretful verdict that things are boring on the edges of the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State' looks like a country or region, but it is the verb 'say'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadly, as a sentence adverb, means unfortunately.

clue.text: Song you once surprisingly rated extremely sexy

parts.note: ye is the old form of you

indicators.note: a surprising arrangement is not the expected order of the letters
the extremes of 'sexy' are its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of sexy

explanation.surface: An old flame was startled to be judged very attractive in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Song' is a bare definition pointing to a famous Beatles track; 'extremely' feeds only the ends of 'sexy' into the mix, not the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is a 1965 Beatles song by Paul McCartney.

clue.text: Informed article goes into popular game making a comeback

indicators.note: coming back means travelling in the opposite direction, so the game reads backwards

parts.note: pool is a cue game played on a table

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece reports that an old favourite game is back in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informed article' reads as a well-researched piece of writing, but 'Informed' is the definition and 'article' is just THE.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: someone in the loop is on the circle of people kept up to date, as opposed to being left out of it.

clue.text: Smartens up for Tate visit after a fashion

indicators.note: done after a fashion means done loosely, not in the proper order

explanation.surface: Someone dresses up before going to the Tate gallery.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of London art galleries; 'after a fashion' also suggests fashion and dressing up, which fits the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To titivate is to smarten oneself up.

clue.text: Are confused in choice of surgical intervention

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled out of order

explanation.surface: Patients are bewildered when asked to pick a kind of surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are confused' reads as people being bewildered, but it tells you to jumble the letters of the word 'Are' itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the medical sense: going under the knife is the standard kind of surgical intervention.

clue.text: Forget his ridiculous thinking about the future

indicators.note: a ridiculous arrangement of the letters is an absurd, jumbled one

explanation.surface: Dismissing a man's silly predictions about what lies ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forget' reads as an instruction to ignore him, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the ability to think ahead about the future.

clue.text: In favour of fighting with Germany at the front

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: Supporting a war with Germany leading the charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the front' seems to place Germany first in the answer, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the positional sense: the forward cabin of a plane or the forward line of a team is the one at the front.

clue.text: Horror of soldiers instilled in father

indicators.note: something instilled in a person is put inside them

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A father has an army-bred fear of soldiers drilled into him.
explanation.walkthrough: RE, the Royal Engineers, is a common crossword abbreviation for soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Dread is a feeling of horror or great fear.

clue.text: Increases speed reversing round inside of bend

indicators.note: DEEPS goes round the middle of bend
a car reversing goes backwards, so SPEED reads from its end
the inside of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A driver speeds up while backing round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Increases speed' reads as one phrase about accelerating, but the definition stops at 'Increases'.
explanation.definitionFit: To deepen is to increase in intensity or depth.

clue.text: Elevated part of railway involves developing giant embankments initially

parts.note: R is an abbreviation for railway

indicators.note: the initial letters of the four words before it are kept

parts.note: the first letters of each word

explanation.surface: An engineering note about raised railway track built on huge banks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Involves' looks like a container instruction, but its I is one of the initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ridge is a long raised strip of ground.

clue.text: Have a house in valley outside Welsh capital

indicators.note: 'outside' means surrounding, so the valley word wraps round the letter taken from Welsh

parts.note: a dell is a small wooded valley

indicators.note: a capital letter is the first one of the word

explanation.surface: Owning a home in a valley on the edge of Cardiff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Welsh capital' points to Cardiff, but the capital here is the letter W.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to live there, to have a house there.

clue.text: Gain promotion against worker with seniority

explanation.surface: A worker objects to being passed over for promotion by someone who has been there longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gain promotion' reads as getting a better job, but 'Gain' is the definition and 'promotion' is an advertisement.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: whatever you gain over a rival puts you ahead of them.

clue.text: A short distance in the lead

parts.note: the narrow margin by which a racehorse can win, measured by a part of its body

explanation.surface: A racing commentary: just a little way in front.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a race result, and 'a head' really is the short distance a horse leads by.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a team two goals up in a match is winning, out in front of the other side.

clue.text: More modern part of Brisbane we recommended

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the following words

explanation.surface: A travel tip for the more up-to-date area of Brisbane.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across three words, from the end of Brisbane to the start of recommended.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both comparatives: this year's model is newer and more modern than last year's.

clue.text: Start to assign repairmen on time for a change

indicators.note: the start of 'assign' is its first letter

parts.note: men who mend things are repairmen
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A manager starts sending engineers out on time to vary the routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a change' reads as 'to vary things', but 'for' is the link and 'a change' is the definition; 'repairmen' splits as MEND MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An amendment is a change, especially to a text or law.

clue.text: Said to be correct to send a letter

indicators.note: what is said is heard, not seen, so the spelling can change

parts.note: a word for correct, as in the right answer, spoken aloud and then spelt as a different word

explanation.surface: Someone is told it is proper to put pen to paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said to be correct' reads as a claim of rightness, but it tells you to hear RIGHT and spell it another way.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the correspondence sense: 'do write while you're away' asks for letters.

clue.text: Postponed action to protect deposit

parts.note: to lay something down is to deposit it

explanation.surface: A legal step to safeguard a deposit has been put off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deposit' looks like money in the bank, but it is the verb lay.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a delayed match has been moved to a later date, which is what postponed means.

clue.text: Contracts for psychiatrists

definitions.meaning: a verb here: to contract is to get smaller
shrink is slang for a psychiatrist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Contracts' looks like a legal document, but it is the verb meaning gets smaller; shrink is slang for a psychiatrist.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink is to contract, and shrinks are psychiatrists, from 'headshrinker'.
